page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.2xlarge belongs to the eighth-generation general-purpose family, utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Compute resources comprise 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores, supporting simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing a standard 4.0 GB of memory per allocated vCPU.

In terms of I/O and acceleration, the instance does not feature onboard local storage, operating entirely without bundled NVMe or SSD drives. As a result, disk storage must be provisioned externally through remote block storage volumes. Network capability provides an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

The m8ib.2xlarge instance presents a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio characteristic of general-purpose systems. The dedicated CPU allocation and 3.9 GHz clock frequency deliver stable compute performance without resource contention from burst credits. While the lack of bundled local disks and GPU capabilities limits its utility for high-IOPS local scratch storage or deep learning workloads, its balanced hardware profile makes it effective for enterprise web serving, microservices architectures, relational database management, and containerized backend processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ib.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general purpose virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and Intel x86_64 architecture. The server provides 8 dedicated vCPUs spread over 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. System memory totals 32.0 GB, delivering a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Network connectivity features an 8 Gbps baseline throughput. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent data, and features no dedicated GPU hardware. With its standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation, the instance delivers predictable, dedicated compute capacity suitable for enterprise application tiers, intermediate data processing, backend microservices, software development environments, and general-purpose production workloads that do not demand dedicated hardware accelerators or local NVMe storage.
